About Priroda¶

Priroda (Russian for “nature”) is a quantum-chemistry program for molecules written by Dimitri N. Laikov. It began as a fast program for GGA density-functional calculations and grew to cover hybrid DFT, RI-MP2, coupled-cluster methods, TDDFT, a scalar-relativistic Hamiltonian, NMR, and Laikov’s own semiempirical model.

The program is closed-source and has no official manual. The official site offers executables, basis-set files and example inputs, but no prose documentation. The other documents in circulation are unofficial: keyword lists such as the English “Input Summary” (input.txt), and a keyword page and beginner FAQ on a computing-centre wiki. This manual collects those texts, the example files on the official site, test runs of version 25, and twenty years of user experience from Russian-language forums. It is not an official document: the developer has not written or reviewed it. Sources lists what it is based on. To download the program, see Obtaining Priroda.

Main features¶

Density-functional theory

GGA DFT in which the Coulomb and exchange–correlation terms are evaluated with an auxiliary (fitting) basis. This is the source of Priroda’s speed. Every orbital basis comes with a matched fitting basis. GGA DFT has analytic second derivatives.

Hybrid functionals with exact exchange evaluated by the resolution of the identity, under theory=ridft.

Correlated methods

RI-MP2 and, as undocumented or less-used options, conventional MP2–MP4, CCSD and CCSD(T). Gradients exist for MP2, CCSD and CCSD(T).

Excited states

GGA TDDFT with excited-state gradients, so excited-state geometries can be optimized.

Relativistic calculations

A scalar-relativistic Hamiltonian (four=1) with all-electron basis sets and a finite-nucleus model. The user FAQ of one computing centre names this, together with basis sets for the whole periodic table, as what sets Priroda apart. Effective core potentials (SBK) are also available.

Geometry and dynamics

Minimization in redundant internal coordinates, transition-state search, IRC, relaxed scans, Hessians with vibrational analysis and thermochemistry, and molecular dynamics with a thermostat.

Properties

NMR shielding tensors and chemical shifts (also at points in space, for NICS), Hirshfeld and Mulliken charges, bond orders, ESR parameters, critical points of the electron density, Raman intensities, and orbitals and normal modes for Molden.

Semiempirical model

Laikov’s parametrized “QM” model (theory=qm_n3), used for systems of thousands of atoms.

Parallel execution

MPI parallelism. In practice it scales well within one node and poorly beyond it; see Installing and running.

Experienced users report that Priroda is markedly faster than general-purpose programs for routine GGA work. One 2018 comparison found it about three times faster per optimization step than ORCA 4.0 (PBE/cc-pVDZ, one core).

Notes to the table:

  1. A CCSD optimization is shown in a user input. CCSD(T) gradients are implied by the developer’s 2011 note on a bug fix that names the CCSD(T) gradient.

  2. Analytic second derivatives.

  3. Computed by finite differences of the gradient (NUMERICAL COMPUTATION OF SECOND DERIVATIVES), which takes many gradient calculations. Shown for ridft and rimp2 in version 25 tests; users report CCSD and CCSD(T) Hessians.

  4. Excited-state optimization works, but Priroda has no root following, so the state can switch during the optimization.

  5. NMR works only with theory=dft and a non-hybrid functional; with ridft, version 25 silently computes only the energy. Users report that relativistic (four=1) NMR runs hang.

  6. There is no hybrid TDDFT. See What Priroda does not do.

  7. Excited states at the coupled-cluster level use a different theory= value, ccsdsd (linear-response CCSD, RHF only), whose status is undocumented.

  8. The Hessian of the excited state given by state= (version 25, water, state=1,3): numerical, with two imaginary modes at the ground-state geometry, as expected for an excited state away from its own minimum.

  9. A TDDFT scan of NH3 failed in version 25: the excited-state equations diverged (g= -nan) and the run stopped with 0: write td.XK(…)?. A TDDFT TS search and IRC on the same molecule worked.

The version 25 tests behind the TS, IRC, scan and MD rows used tiny molecules (NH3, water) and short runs, so they show that the combination runs and ends normally, not how well it behaves on real problems.

The scalar-relativistic option four=1 has been used with dft, ridft and rimp2. The full list of theory= values, including the undocumented ones, is in $control theory.

Warning

Hybrid functionals work only with theory=ridft. With theory=dft, older versions silently drop the exact exchange, and newer versions, including version 25, stop right after printing the basis sets with no error message in the output. With theory=tddft, version 25 still runs a hybrid without its exact exchange and gives wrong energies with no warning. See $control theory.

What Priroda does not do¶

Check this list before planning a project around Priroda.

No use of point-group symmetry in older versions

Older versions always run in C1. A symmetric starting structure stays symmetric during optimization, so a Hessian is needed to show whether it is a minimum. Newer outputs (v13 onwards) print a detected point group, and the official 2023–2025 example inputs use sym=1 in $molecule and $optimize. These options are not documented. In version 25 tests, $molecule sym=1,0.01 symmetrized the structure and $optimize sym=1 kept the symmetry during the optimization; each option alone does only half of this. See $molecule sym and $optimize symmetry.

No continuum solvation

No version has a continuum solvent model. Solvent can only be included as explicit molecules.

No D3 or other empirical dispersion correction

The developer has declined to add one (relayed from correspondence). Users add Grimme’s D3 a posteriori with the external dftd3 program. The 2023–2025 functionals LPBEVV and LPBEVVV may include dispersion, but this is inferred from their test systems and not documented.

No periodic systems

Priroda handles molecules and clusters only.

No dummy atoms, so no counterpoise (BSSE) correction

Ghost centres cannot be placed in $molecule. For NICS, give the probe points in $nmr points instead.

No hybrid TDDFT

TDDFT is GGA only. A hybrid functional with theory=tddft does not give hybrid TDDFT: version 25 drops the exact exchange without a warning, and the energies are wrong.

Other gaps reported by users:

  • no spin–orbit coupling, so no phosphorescence calculations;

  • no multireference methods (CASSCF, MRCI, CASPT2) that users could get working;

  • no freezing of atoms in Cartesian space; only internal coordinates can be fixed ($optimize fix);

  • no general job chaining in one input: task=optimize+hessian is the only combined task, and two task= lines run only the first.

Version history¶

Priroda numbers its versions with integers and prints the build date in the output banner, for example Priroda 13 (2013.01.10). Energies differ slightly between versions, so keep every calculation you compare on one version.

Banner program Priroda version 2.10. Had task=optimize+hessian.

4

2004.09.14 (v4.07)

The finite-nucleus model changed between versions 3 and 4, so pre-v4 relativistic basis sets must not be used with v4 and later.

5

—

Version described by the keyword reference on the KNC wiki. Introduced the systematic L basis sets. Hybrid RI-DFT was implemented in November 2004.

6

2006.08.20

Long the most widely used version: 32- and 64-bit Linux builds with MPI, and a Windows build (p6.exe). optimize+hessian was removed. Parallel Hessians use at most 2 cores.

2016–2018

The Windows build runs in parallel from version 16. Version 17 runs Hessians on 4 or more cores. Around 2016 the developer removed limits on SCF memory allocation and on the system size for Hessians.

23

2023.06.22

Newest numbered version reported by users (2024). New functionals LPBEVV and LPBEVVV.

25

2025.02.28

Banner Priroda 25 (2025.02.28). The version used for the test runs behind this manual. Its date matches the p4_d build on the official site; p_l is dated 2025-04-14. The 2025 example inputs use theory=DFT_n4.

Version numbers missing from the table (3, 12, 18–22, 24) do not appear in any source. The Russian file Dft_ansi.txt describes Priroda’s predecessor, whose input had the groups $control, $coordinates, $basis, $auxiliary, $guess, $SCF, $search, $force and $hessian. Version 25 reads none of $coordinates, $auxiliary, $search, $force and $hessian; the geometry now goes in $molecule, and optimization settings in $optimize.

How to cite¶

Priroda has no single program paper for the current version. Users cite the papers below; the first three are the list given by the KNC wiki FAQ and repeated in the forums.

Program:

  • D. N. Laikov, Yu. A. Ustynyuk. PRIRODA-04: a quantum-chemical program suite. New possibilities in the study of molecular systems with the application of parallel computing. Russ. Chem. Bull., Int. Ed. 54 (2005) 820–826. Russian original: Izv. Akad. Nauk, Ser. Khim. 2005, No. 3, 804–810.

Density-fitting DFT (cite for any DFT calculation):

  • D. N. Laikov. Fast evaluation of density functional exchange-correlation terms using the expansion of the electron density in auxiliary basis sets. Chem. Phys. Lett. 281 (1997) 151–156.

L-family basis sets (L1, L2, L11, …):

  • D. N. Laikov. A new class of atomic basis functions for accurate electronic structure calculations of molecules. Chem. Phys. Lett. 416 (2005) 116–120.

The 3z basis set, which has no journal paper:

  • D. N. Laikov. “Development of an economical approach to the density functional calculation of molecules and its application to complex chemical problems”. PhD dissertation, Moscow State University, 2000 (in Russian).

Scalar-relativistic DFT (four=1):

  • D. N. Laikov. An implementation of the scalar relativistic density functional theory for molecular calculations with Gaussian basis sets. DFT2000 Conference, Menton, France, 2000.

Semiempirical QM model (theory=qm_n*):

  • D. N. Laikov. A new parametrizable model of molecular electronic structure. J. Chem. Phys. 135 (2011) 134120, doi:10.1063/1.3646498.

For version 6, users cited the program itself as “D. N. Laikov, PRIRODA, Electronic Structure Code, Version 6, 2006”. A 2014 forum suggestion adds Laikov’s home page, http://rad.chem.msu.ru/~laikov/, as the reference for the current version.

Also cite the original papers for the functional, and for the Hamiltonian and nuclear model if you use four=1. $dft functional and $control four give them.
